title: Quraysh: fed and safe
hookLine: let them worship the Lord of this House who fed them and made them safe (Surah 106)
last: AL-MA'UN — THE SMALL KINDNESS IS THE TEST.

cards: Two questions. Is there food today? Am I safe today?
For some people, right now, they're the first two thoughts of the morning. For others they're answered so completely they've stopped sounding like questions.

The fridge hums, the door locks, and nobody thinks about either. Today's surah is named for a tribe, the Prophet's own, and it reminds them of exactly those two things. Four lines, and a list of just two gifts.

teach.b: Quraysh was the tribe that ran Mecca, the Prophet Muhammad's own people. Mecca sits in a dry valley; elsewhere the Qur'an calls it a valley without crops. What it had was the Ka'bah, the House, and trade.

Commentators explain that Quraysh sent two great caravans a year: in winter south to Yemen, in summer north to Syria. The surah's first word, ilaf, they explain as the custom and security of those journeys.
Other tribes let the caravans pass, the commentators say, because Quraysh were the keepers of the House. So a desert town had grain, cloth and peace.

teach.h: FED AGAINST HUNGER, SAFE FROM FEAR.
teach.b: Then the surah turns, in Pickthall's words: So let them worship the Lord of this House, Who hath fed them against hunger and hath made them safe from fear. Notice the logic. It doesn't threaten.
It reminds. You're eating. You're safe.
Where do you think that came from? Commentators read this surah together with the one before it in the book, about the elephant, which comes tomorrow.
And that closes another week of short surahs: al-Ikhlas, an uncle whose kinship didn't save him, winning humbly, a boundary without a threat, abundance for a grieving man, the bucket and the pot.
And now, bread, and a night without fear.

how: Surah Quraysh is recited in the prayers like other short surahs, and many Muslims recall it when giving thanks for food and safety.

o: the Prophet's tribe, keepers of the House in Mecca
the dry valley around the Ka'bah in Mecca
the trade caravans that ran from Mecca to Syria

games.q: what's inside the surah — tap the pairs.
p: the custom and security of the journeys

s: it reminds them: you were fed against hunger and made safe from fear.
it sat in a dry valley; its food came through trade.
Quraysh was the Prophet's own tribe
they ran Mecca and were keepers of the House.

games.q: your town is fed and safe, year after year, thanks to caravans and peace. what does the surah say to do with that?
o: worship the Lord of this House who fed you and made you safe
games.why: the surah turns the gifts into a reason, not a boast: let them worship the Lord of this House (106:3–4).

practice: Think about your last meal and trace it back: who cooked it, who sold it, who drove it, who grew it. Then think about where you're sitting, the locked door, the quiet street, and who keeps it that way.
Let the two words rest on your breath, fed on the in-breath, safe on the out-breath; if you pray, you can thank Allah for both, in your own words.
